notes: The first cross-language pair of this generation: a c@1 program as a bit-vector machine. T embeds the c@1 interpreter's own front end verbatim and encodes the elaborated CFG it executes — one btor2 state for the program counter and for every slot (arrays as btor2 array states, broadcast-0 init, bounds-guarded reads/writes mirroring the interpreter's out-of-range rule), one btor2 input per havoc site in site order, absorbing HALT/ERR codes past the locations, bad = (pc == ERR). Every CFG node is one transition, so bad AND depth carry exactly and a universal claim at btor2 bound k is a bound-k fact at the C level — no bound_cap. Both languages name the observables identically, so maps is the identity. Lam re-runs the builder to reproduce the site-to-input-node map (a pure function of the program) and carries a btor2 witness stimulus back as a renaming. The division family, shift saturation, and frame discipline agree by construction with btor2@2/@3 semantics. Out of the pair's fragment: nonzero global array initializers (btor2 array init is broadcast-only). Pre-admission evidence: the square held on 1188 of 1188 random dual-keyed stimulus runs across all 594 in-fragment SV-COMP tasks (validate_pair.py, /Users/ck/svcomp).
